key_insight: A six-qubit hybrid quantum–classical autoencoder reconstructs images using measured Pauli correlators and a classical neural decoder.
engineering_relevance: The architecture runs on current IBM quantum hardware without retraining, demonstrating a small-scale implementation rather than quantum advantage.
method: Split images into patches and compress each patch as a matrix product state.
Extract quantum features with six qubits arranged in a line or grid, then decode using features and patch position.
Train with a learnable physics-inspired energy term; average grid-model features for exact rotation/reflection equivariance.
evidence_signal: Trained per image across six public datasets, PCAE2D achieved 25.8–41.6 dB PSNR; five trained models achieved 25.90–31.52 dB on IBM hardware without retraining.
watch_item: Generalization evidence uses a formula-based feature surrogate on unseen CIFAR-10 images, so it does not establish end-to-end quantum generalization or advantage.
paper_title: Hybrid Quantum--Classical Pauli-Correlator Architecture for Image Reconstruction
